highlights.title: Tongariro Alpine Crossing
highlights.description: New Zealand's most iconic day hike — 20km across an active volcanic plateau. Red Crater, emerald alpine lakes, ash fields, and a summit at 1,886m. Challenging, unforgettable, and deeply surreal.
highlights.image_query: Tongariro Alpine Crossing volcanic New Zealand

highlights.title: Milford Sound: Fly-Cruise-Fly
highlights.description: Forty minutes over Fiordland's snowcapped peaks by light plane, then a 1h45m cruise through the fjord past waterfalls and resident seals. The return flight over the Southern Alps seals it as the most spectacular day in the country.
highlights.image_query: Milford Sound Fiordland aerial New Zealand

highlights.title: Nevis Bungee — 134m
highlights.description: The highest bungy jump in New Zealand: a 134-metre drop off a cable car suspended above the Nevis River gorge, with 8.5 seconds of freefall. Not a tourist gimmick — this is the real thing.
highlights.image_query: Nevis Bungee Queenstown New Zealand gorge

highlights.title: Rotorua: Māori Culture
highlights.description: Te Puia's working Māori arts institute erupts beside the Pōhutu Geyser. The Whakarewarewa living village is exactly that — families still cook in geothermal pools. One of the few places in the world where ancient culture is genuinely alive, not performed.
highlights.image_query: Rotorua Te Puia geyser Maori culture New Zealand

highlights.title: Lomani Island, Fiji
highlights.description: Seventeen rooms on a private patch of Malolo Lailai Island — adults-only, intimate enough that staff learn your names on day one. Daily guided reef snorkel trips, kava ceremonies, and evening beach dinners. The post-adventure exhale.
highlights.image_query: Lomani Island Resort Fiji beach bungalow

highlights.title: Wānaka + Roys Peak
highlights.description: Forty-five minutes from Queenstown, Wānaka is quieter, prettier, and completely different in character. Roys Peak is a 5-hour return summit hike with one of the most photographed panoramas in New Zealand — the Southern Alps and Lake Wānaka from 1,578m.
highlights.estimated_cost: Free hike · Rippon vineyard tasting from free
highlights.image_query: Roys Peak Wanaka New Zealand summit lake

highlights.title: Central Otago Wine Harvest
highlights.description: March–April is harvest season in the Gibbston Valley — the world's southernmost Pinot Noir region. Rolling schist canyon, boutique cellar doors, and vineyard lunches that stretch into the afternoon.
highlights.image_query: Central Otago Gibbston Valley vineyard Queenstown

highlights.title: Walter Peak Dinner Cruise
highlights.description: Board the vintage TSS Earnslaw steamship at Queenstown's pier, cross Lake Wakatipu to the high-country Walter Peak farm, and sit down to a gourmet BBQ dinner as the Remarkables turn pink at sunset.
highlights.image_query: Walter Peak TSS Earnslaw Lake Wakatipu Queenstown sunset

accommodation.name: Koura Lodge
accommodation.description: Boutique lakeside B&B, 8 rooms all facing Lake Rotorua with private deck access, outdoor hot tub and sauna. 5 minutes from Te Puia and the geothermal zones. Nir gets uninterrupted lake panoramas; Sarah gets an owner-run property that doesn't feel like a hotel.

accommodation.name: Tongariro Crossing Lodge
accommodation.description: Built for exactly this purpose — shuttle departs from the door, spa pool on-site for post-hike recovery. New garden suites opened 2025. Not a luxury lodge, but perfectly positioned and extremely well-reviewed for the crossing experience.

accommodation.name: Kamana Lakehouse
accommodation.description: Independently owned boutique hotel with the Remarkables and Lake Wakatipu panorama as the headline — Nir's #1 priority met immediately. Five minutes from Queenstown's dining strip, so evenings are easy. Genuine boutique feel, not a chain in disguise.

accommodation.name: Lomani Island Resort
accommodation.description: Adults-only, 17 rooms total — this is genuinely intimate. Daily guided snorkel trips to different reef spots are included and consistently the most-praised aspect of a stay. Food is exceptional (multiple 2025–26 reviews: 'spectacular,' 'restaurant-quality'). Kava ceremonies, private beach dinners, and genuine Fijian hospitality.

flights.airline: Fiji Airways / Air New Zealand (via AKL)

itinerary.morning: Long-haul arrival from Chicago. Clear customs, grab the rental car. Coffee from a good Auckland café — flat whites are a different league here.
itinerary.afternoon: Check into the transit hotel near the waterfront. Walk the Viaduct Harbour. Light grocery run for snacks and tomorrow's road trip provisions.
itinerary.evening: Early dinner — something simple and local. Early night. The adventure starts properly tomorrow.

itinerary.morning: Hit the road early — 2.5 hours south to Rotorua. Stop in Tirau for flat whites and the world's most surreal small-town corrugated-iron buildings.
itinerary.afternoon: Wai-O-Tapu Thermal Landscape — the Champagne Pool (vivid orange silica edges), Artist's Palette (green and yellow sulphur formations), Lady Knox Geyser. 2–3 hours self-guided. $27/person. 30 minutes from Rotorua centre.
itinerary.evening: Polynesian Spa — 12 geothermal mineral pools set over Lake Rotorua, some dating back to 1882. Deluxe Double Dipper includes both the historic Pavilion pools and the cliff-edge Lake Spa pools. $66/person. Book the 5pm–7pm slot for golden hour.

itinerary.morning: Te Puia — the working Māori arts institute. Watch master carvers and weavers at work, then catch the 90-minute guided experience including the Pōhutu Geyser and a cultural performance (haka, poi, waiata). $72/person. Book the 9am slot to beat tour groups.
itinerary.afternoon: Whakarewarewa Living Village — unlike Te Puia, this village is still fully inhabited. Guides are residents. Families cook in the thermal pools. 1-hour guided tour. $24/person. This is the more authentic of the two — fewer theatrics, more real.
itinerary.evening: Dinner on the Rotorua waterfront strip. Try Atticus Finch for craft beer and shared plates, or Eat Streat for local flavour and open-air atmosphere.

itinerary.morning: Pack up and drive south toward Taupo (1 hour). Stop at Huka Falls — the most visited natural site in New Zealand and genuinely worth it. A turquoise, 220,000-litre-per-second rush through a narrow canyon. Free, 5-minute walk from the car park.
itinerary.afternoon: Check into Tongariro Crossing Lodge. Early to bed is optional — the better option is the lakeside Taupo dining strip for a long, relaxed dinner.
itinerary.evening: Early dinner, early sleep. The shuttle departs at 6:30am.

itinerary.morning: 6:30am shuttle from the lodge drops you at Mangatepopo trailhead. The opening hour crosses a vast lava field toward the volcanoes — Mt Ngauruhoe rising on your right (the original Mt Doom). Red Crater summit at 1,886m.
itinerary.afternoon: The descent from Red Crater passes the glowing emerald Emerald Lakes — thermal-tinted and completely surreal at altitude. 20.2km total, 6–8 hours. Shuttle picks you up from Ketetahi end by 3pm.
itinerary.evening: Back at the lodge by 4pm. Into the spa pool immediately. Dinner in the village. Legs will complain. That's correct.

itinerary.morning: Drive back toward Auckland (or Rotorua Airport). Domestic flight to Queenstown — 1h20m, with aerial views of the North Island from above. Air New Zealand domestic is reliable.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive Queenstown. Drop bags at Kamana Lakehouse — the Remarkables visible from check-in. Walk the waterfront along Lake Wakatipu.
itinerary.evening: Fergburger. Yes, the queue. Yes, it's worth it. Craft beer at Altitude Brewing after. Early night — tomorrow is one of the best days of the trip.

itinerary.day_theme: The Most Spectacular Day in New Zealand
itinerary.morning: Queenstown Airport, 8am flight over Fiordland. The aerial approach to Milford Sound — snowcapped peaks, glacial valleys, no roads below — is itself worth the price. Land at Milford aerodrome.
itinerary.afternoon: 1h45m cruise through the fjord. Stirling Falls up close, fur seals on the rocks, bottlenose dolphins if the weather behaves. The scale is incomprehensible in photos — you understand it only from the water.
itinerary.evening: Return flight over the Southern Alps. Back in Queenstown by 3pm. Dinner at a waterfront restaurant — Finz Seafood & Grill for a blow-out, or Madam Woo for something more relaxed.

itinerary.morning: Nevis Bungee, 8am slot. 134m platform suspended from a cable car above the Nevis Gorge. 8.5 seconds of freefall. Includes return transfer from Queenstown, photo package, and certificate. $237/person.
itinerary.afternoon: Dart River Wilderness Jet Boat — 90 minutes, up to 90km through Mt Aspiring National Park. 80mph through canyon walls on a river where Lord of the Rings was filmed. $106/person.
itinerary.evening: TSS Earnslaw and the Walter Peak Dinner Cruise. Board the 1912 vintage coal-fired steamship at the Queenstown pier, cross Lake Wakatipu, gourmet BBQ at the high-country farm, back by 9:30pm. $119/person. Book ahead — sells out.

itinerary.morning: 45-minute drive to Wānaka. Arrive by 7am for Roys Peak — 5–6 hours return, 1,578m summit, the most iconic panorama in the South Island. Free. Trekking poles useful.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend into Wānaka town. Rippon Vineyard cellar door tasting — 4–6 Pinot Noir wines on a lakeside deck with the peak behind you, by appointment. From free.
itinerary.evening: Drive back to Queenstown (45 min) in time for dinner. Try Rata for a celebratory South Island meal.

itinerary.morning: Central Otago half-day wine tour. Gibbston Valley schist canyon, 3–4 boutique cellar doors, vineyard lunch included. March is harvest — you may walk the rows during picking. $141/person.
itinerary.afternoon: Back in Queenstown by 3pm. Lake walk, final afternoon in the adventure capital. Pack for Fiji.
itinerary.evening: Celebratory last-night-in-NZ dinner. Botswana Butchery on the waterfront — South Island rack of lamb.

itinerary.morning: Fly Queenstown → Nadi via Auckland. Total journey time approximately 6–7 hours including the connection.
itinerary.afternoon: Arrive Nadi. Fast boat from Port Denarau Marina to Malolo Lailai Island — 45 minutes across open turquoise water. Welcome cocktail on arrival at Lomani.
itinerary.evening: Explore the 17-room resort, which takes about 15 minutes. Watch the sunset over the lagoon from the beach. The pace has officially changed.

itinerary.morning: Lomani's guided morning snorkel trip to the outer reef — multiple coral and fish species, guided to the best spots. Included in the room rate.
itinerary.afternoon: Beach time. Stand-up paddleboarding from the shore. Couples' spa treatment (book on arrival).
itinerary.evening: Kava ceremony with staff — a genuine Fijian cultural exchange, not a staged show. Dinner on the beach.

itinerary.morning: Catamaran day-sail to a neighbouring island. Snorkel, swim, drift. Lunch on the boat.
itinerary.afternoon: Return to Lomani. Long afternoon on the beach. Read. Nap. Do nothing at all.
itinerary.evening: Sunset cruise on the resort's boat. Best cocktails of the trip. Private beach dinner if booked as part of the honeymoon package.

itinerary.morning: Final snorkel or sunrise swim. Last coffee on the beach. Boat back to Port Denarau by 11am.
itinerary.afternoon: Nadi airport. Afternoon departure NAN → LAX/SFO → ORD.
itinerary.evening: Overnight flight home. Arrive Chicago Day 15.

bonus_activities.title: Kaikōura: Sperm Whale Watching
bonus_activities.description: Sperm whales are resident year-round off Kaikōura, 2.5h north of Christchurch. 95% success rate, 80% refund if no whale. Add a day between Queenstown and Fiji if the routing allows via CHC.

bonus_activities.title: Skydive over Lake Taupo
bonus_activities.description: Jump at 15,000ft over the lake and Tongariro volcanoes — one of the most dramatic skydive views in the world. Nir's profile written all over it. Add on Day 4 if energy allows after the drive.

bonus_activities.title: Private Guided Tongariro Crossing
bonus_activities.description: Upgrade the shuttle ($33/person) to a private guided crossing with Adrift Tongariro or Walk into Luxury — set your own pace, expert volcanic geology commentary, and no logistics stress on the big day. Worth it for a honeymoon if budget allows.

bonus_activities.title: Heli-Hike into the Southern Alps
bonus_activities.description: Helicopter drop into the backcountry from Queenstown — glacier landing or remote alpine terrain that's otherwise inaccessible. The premium version of 'adventure access' that fits Nir's splurge profile exactly.

bonus_activities.title: Swim with Dolphins — Kaikōura
bonus_activities.description: Dusky dolphins in pods of hundreds. Wetsuit provided, 3.5 hours total. DOC permits limit spots — book immediately when dates are confirmed. Add with the whale watching day for a full Kaikōura wildlife stop.
